item.text: {"rubric":[{"claim_id":"c1","claim_type":"core","weight":35,"statement":"`Signature.dump_state()` serializes the signature instructions and, for each field, only the field's `prefix` and `desc` metadata (with `desc` written under the `description` key).","span_ids":["s1"]},{"claim_id":"c2","claim_type":"core","weight":40,"statement":"`Signature.load_state()` starts from a deep copy of the receiving signature's current fields and only overwrites `instructions`, `prefix`, and `desc`, so serialized state does not replace other field properties such as the receiver's annotations/types or defaults.","span_ids":["s1","s2"]},{"claim_id":"c3","claim_type":"core","weight":15,"statement":"`Predict.load_state()` restores the signature by calling `self.signature.load_state(state[\"signature\"])` on the predictor's existing signature, so loading into another predictor/signature uses the receiver signature as the base rather than reconstructing the saved signature class.","span_ids":["s3"]},{"claim_id":"c4","claim_type":"supporting","weight":10,"statement":"The tests confirm that when a saved predictor/signature is loaded into a different signature class, changed instructions and field text/prefix are overwritten until the receiving signature's dumped state matches the original saved metadata.","span_ids":["s4","s5"]}],"evidence":[{"span_id":"s1","path":"dspy/signatures/signature.py","start_line":487,"end_line":497},{"span_id":"s2","path":"dspy/signatures/signature.py","start_line":499,"end_line":508},{"span_id":"s3","path":"dspy/predict/predict.py","start_line":103,"end_line":111},{"span_id":"s4","path":"tests/predict/test_predict.py","start_line":79,"end_line":85},{"span_id":"s5","path":"tests/predict/test_predict.py","start_line":215,"end_line":236}]}
